sources.entry: Dippy by Lily Dayton - Auto-approve safe bash commands using AST-based parsing, while prompting for destructive operations. Solves permission fatigue without disabling safety. Supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Cursor.

summary.one_liner: Dippy is a shell command hook for Claude Code that auto-approves safe bash commands and prompts for destructive ones, built on a hand-written bash parser.
summary.what_it_does:
Dippy runs as a shell command hook that Claude Code invokes before each Bash tool call. It parses the command with Parable, the author's own hand-written bash parser, and auto-approves read-only or otherwise safe commands such as ls, git status, cat, and cloud or container inspection calls. It handles pipelines, chains with && and pipes, safe redirects like 2>/dev/null, and command substitution. Commands that write files, mutate state, or are destructive (for example git stash drop, npm unpublish, kubectl delete, or a rm -rf chain) are blocked so the user is prompted. Users can add config rules in ~/.dippy/config or a project .dippy file, including deny rules with custom messages intended to steer the assistant. The README also says it supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Cursor.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="how_to_run">["brew tap ldayton/dippy", "brew install dippy", "git clone <repository URL (not given in README)>", "Add a PreToolUse hook with matcher \"Bash\" and command \"dippy\" to ~/.claude/settings.json (or use /hooks)", "If installed manually, point the hook command at /path/to/Dippy/bin/dippy-hook", "Optionally add deny rules to ~/.dippy/config or a project .dippy file"]
use_cases: Stop Claude Code from asking approval for ls, git status, and cat
Let an AI coding assistant run read-only shell commands unattended
Block destructive shell commands while keeping safe ones automatic
Steer an AI agent with custom deny messages when it runs a disallowed command
Prevent agents from writing secrets files or using shell redirects to write files
Speed up agent-driven development without turning off permissions
notable: Uses an AST-based bash parser (Parable) written by the author, with no external dependencies
Deny rules can carry custom messages that tell the AI what to do instead
Approves whole chains and pipelines, but blocks the entire chain if one part is unsafe
Config via ~/.dippy/config globally and .dippy per project
Claims support for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Cursor
caveats: README gives no git clone URL for manual install, only a placeholder
Full documentation and extensions are only referenced via an external wiki
Claims of up to 40% faster development are the author's marketing, not measured here
Blocked commands still require manual approval, so safety depends on the rule set
